short: Three times prime minister, through the General Strike and the abdication crisis.
full:
Stanley Baldwin led three governments between 1923 and 1937 and dominated Conservative politics for a generation. He lost an election in 1923 by campaigning for tariffs, returned in 1924, and faced the General Strike of May 1926, when some 1.7 million workers came out in support of the miners. The strike collapsed after nine days; the Trade Disputes Act of 1927 made sympathetic strikes illegal.

He served under Ramsay MacDonald in the National Government formed during the slump, then took the premiership a third time in 1935. That ministry passed the Government of India Act, began rearmament slowly in the face of a pacifist electorate, and handled the abdication of Edward VIII in December 1936 with a deftness that briefly made him popular. He retired in May 1937. Later criticism, much of it from Churchill, held him responsible for Britain's unreadiness for war.
